title: Capability-based sandboxing
description: Capabilities are unforgeable tokens of authority: a sandboxed process holds capabilities only for what it's allowed (this file, that socket), enforced by the kernel or language runtime. No ambient authority — the sandbox can't reach what it was never given. seL4, Capsicum, and object-capability languages build on this.
method: Issue fine-grained capabilities at spawn; the kernel/runtime checks each access; no capability = no access, by construction.
usage: Grant least privilege at spawn; capabilities are the API — design around them.

demo.code:
print('sandbox caps: [read /data/in.csv] (only)')
print('open("/etc/passwd"): DENIED (no capability) — by construction')

title: Proof-carrying sandbox policies
description: Sandbox policies (seccomp filters, capability sets) ship with proofs that they enforce the intended isolation: the policy is verified against a model of the kernel interface before installation. A misconfigured filter is caught by proof, not by exploit.
method: Model the policy; prove it denies the forbidden actions; install only proved policies; re-prove on change.
usage: Verify sandbox policies like code; the proof is the configuration review.

demo.code:
print('seccomp policy: 312 syscalls analyzed, 41 allowed')
print('proof: no allowed path to execve -> INSTALLED')

title: Multi-party sandboxed computation
description: Parties contribute private inputs to a sandboxed joint computation: the sandbox runs under MPC or in a TEE, each party attests it, and the result is released only when all attestations verify. Nobody trusts anyone's machine — they trust the attested sandbox.
method: Deploy the computation in an attested sandbox/TEE; parties verify attestation; inputs contributed; result released on consensus.
usage: Use for joint computations among distrustful parties; verify attestations independently.

demo.code:
print('3 parties attest sandbox m7f2 -> all verify OK')
print('private inputs in; joint result out; no party saw others\' inputs')

title: Deterministic sandbox replay
description: Sandbox executions are recorded (inputs, nondeterministic events) and replayable deterministically — a sandbox that misbehaves can be rewound and dissected. The recording is also the audit trail: exactly what the untrusted code did, step by step.
method: Record inputs and nondeterminism; replay deterministically for analysis; the recording is the audit log.
usage: Record sandbox runs handling untrusted input; replay for incident analysis.

demo.code:
print('sandbox run recorded: 14,204 syscalls')
print('incident: replay pinpoints the exploit attempt at syscall 9,001')

title: Sandbox escape detection
description: Assume escape attempts: monitors watch for sandbox-boundary violations (unexpected syscalls, capability use anomalies, timing side channels) and kill the sandbox on detection. The sandbox is a containment that reports its own breaches — defense in depth around the boundary.
method: Monitor boundary crossings; anomaly-detect on syscall patterns; kill on violation; alert as security incident.
usage: Monitor every sandbox; treat escape attempts as incidents, not bugs.

demo.code:
print('sandbox attempted ptrace() (not in policy)')
print('KILLED + security incident opened')

title: Compartmentalized crypto services
description: Split crypto services into compartments (key handling, protocol logic, I/O) with capabilities between them — a bug in the protocol parser can't reach the keys. Compartmentalization (CHERI, enclave-per-service) limits blast radius by architecture, enforced cryptographically.
method: Compartment per function; capabilities for inter-compartment calls; a compromised compartment can't escalate.
usage: Compartmentalize by privilege level; the key compartment should be tiny.

demo.code:
print('compartments: [parser] [protocol] [key-vault]')
print('parser exploited -> cannot reach key-vault (no capability)')

title: Egress-filtered crypto sandboxes
description: The sandbox's network is a cryptographic boundary: all egress through an encrypting proxy that only allows attested destinations, with payloads logged (in ciphertext) for audit. Data can't leave except through the approved, observed channel.
method: Proxy all egress; allowlist destinations; log encrypted payloads; block everything else by default.
usage: Default-deny egress; the allowlist is the security policy — review it.

demo.code:
print('egress attempt: api.vendor.com (allowlisted) -> PROXIED + logged')
print('egress attempt: evil.com -> DENIED (default)')

title: Time-boxed cryptographic leases
description: Sandbox authority expires: capabilities and decryption keys carry leases, and when the lease lapses the sandbox loses access automatically — no revocation round-trip needed. Time-boxing bounds the damage of a compromised sandbox to the lease window.
method: Issue short-lived capabilities/keys; renew on health checks; expiry is automatic and total.
usage: Keep leases short; automate renewal; expiry must need no cooperation from the sandbox.

demo.code:
import time
lease_exp = time.time() + 300
print(f'capability lease expires in 300s')
print('compromised sandbox at 301s: authority GONE (no revocation needed)')
